question: What is loop engineering?
answer:
- Loop engineering creates an external, bounded, reusable loop specification that a human designs and hands to an agent harness, enabling the agent to find, run, verify, and remember work without a human in each step . [chunk_1]
- A loop specification assembles five reusable pieces and an external memory . [chunk_2]
- The trigger starts the agent; the goal and verification decide whether the work is done; the result is logged and persisted in memory; the loop repeats until a terminal state, which is governed by a budget ceiling or a no‑progress detector . [chunk_3]
- A loop is only a loop when feedback from one iteration changes the next action . [chunk_3]
- Practitioners have shifted from prompting agents directly to designing loops that prompt them, and a public Loop Library provides reusable loop artifacts . [chunk_4]
- A loop is inappropriate when the next action does not change with new feedback . [chunk_5]

The first task is to fix the object of study, because the word “loop” carries at least three meanings. An ordinary programming loop is plain control flow. The internal cycle of an agent, the model running tools in a while over a stop condition, is the perceive-act-observe machinery that frameworks from ReAct [50] onward formalized; it is part of the harness and it exists whether or not anyone designs it. The harness supplies the engine; loop engineering writes the pilot. We situate the practice as a new layer in a progression (Figure 1).3 Prompt engineering asked how to ask. Context engineering asked what the agent knows and remembers. Harness engineering asked what environment, tools and limits the agent has. Loop engineering asks what system one builds so the agent finds, runs, verifies and remembers the work without a human in the middle of each step. Each layer subsumes the previous one rather than discarding it
